rows.text: Every tax in this deck is symmetrical on paper and one-sided in practice, because Grand Arbiter refunds you. Sphere of Resistance costs everyone {1} more — and gives you {1} back on every white or blue spell you cast. Stack three or four of those effects and the table simply stops being able to cast anything, while your own hand gets cheaper.

rows.name: Grand Arbiter Augustin IV
rows.text: your white spells and your blue spells each cost {1} less; theirs all cost {1} more. Nearly every card in the deck is white or blue, so the discount applies to almost everything you do.

rows.name: Sphere of Resistance
rows.text: everything costs {1} more. With Arbiter out, your white and blue spells are back to full price and theirs are up two.

rows.name: Thalia, Guardian of Thraben
rows.text: the same tax aimed at noncreature spells, on a first-striking body.

rows.name: Lodestone Golem
rows.text: nonartifact spells cost {1} more, and it is a 5/3 that actually attacks.

rows.name: God-Pharaoh's Statue
rows.text: two more on every spell they cast, plus a drain each turn — it is a clock and a lock in one card.

rows.name: Sapphire Medallion
rows.text: another {1} off your blue spells, stacking with Arbiter.

rows.name: Pearl Medallion
rows.text: and the white half. With Arbiter plus a Medallion, two-mana spells are free.

rows.name: Aura of Silence
rows.text: their artifacts and enchantments cost two more, and it eats one on the way out.

rows.name: Spelltithe Enforcer
rows.text: they pay {1} per spell or lose a permanent. With the taxes above, the {1} is not always available.
The tax package makes each spell expensive; this package makes it their ONLY spell. Together they end games.

rows.name: Rule of Law
rows.text: one spell per turn, each. The enchantment version, hardest to remove.

rows.name: Archon of Emeria
rows.text: the same, on a 2/3 flier, plus their nonbasics enter tapped.

rows.name: Eidolon of Rhetoric
rows.text: a third copy on a 1/4 that blocks well.

rows.name: Ethersworn Canonist
rows.text: one nonartifact spell each, which is strictly better for you than for a table not built on artifacts.

rows.name: Deafening Silence
rows.text: one noncreature spell each, for one mana, and it never affects your creature deployment.

rows.name: Sanctum Prelate
rows.text: name the number the table is built around — usually two or three — and those spells simply cannot be cast at all.

rows.name: Lavinia, Azorius Renegade
rows.text: they cannot cast noncreature spells above their land count, and anything cast for free is countered outright. She blanks Force of Will, ritual-fuelled combo turns and cascade cheats.

rows.name: Teferi, Time Raveler
rows.text: they can only act at sorcery speed. No instant-speed removal, no counterspells on your turn.

rows.name: Jin-Gitaxias, Progress Tyrant
rows.text: counters the first artifact, instant or sorcery each opponent casts each turn AND copies yours. Once a one-spell-per-turn effect is out, the one spell they get is the one Jin-Gitaxias counters.

rows.name: Grand Abolisher
rows.text: they cannot cast anything at all during your turn.

rows.name: Myrel, Shield of Argive
rows.text: the same lockout on a body that also builds an army every attack.

rows.name: Silence
rows.text: one mana for a whole turn of protection. Cast it before the combo turn or before the wrath.

rows.name: Counterspell
rows.text: the clean answer that never rots in hand.

rows.name: Mana Drain
rows.text: counter, and the floating mana deploys two more prison pieces.

rows.name: Dovin's Veto
rows.text: uncounterable, for the counter war you cannot afford to lose.

rows.name: Force of Negation
rows.text: free on their turn, which matters when you have tapped out to deploy.

rows.name: Swan Song
rows.text: one mana, and a 2/2 Bird is nothing against Ghostly Prison.

rows.name: Ghostly Prison
rows.text: they pay {2} per attacker or go hit somebody else. In a pod, that is usually enough on its own.

rows.name: Blind Obedience
rows.text: their creatures and artifacts arrive tapped, so no surprise blocker and no haste kill, and extort drains them every time you cast.

rows.name: Linvala, Keeper of Silence
rows.text: no creature activated abilities for them. Mana dorks, sac outlets and tutor creatures all stop.

rows.name: Grafdigger's Cage
rows.text: nothing comes back from graveyards or libraries.

rows.name: Rest in Peace
rows.text: the full version, and this deck never uses its own graveyard.

rows.name: Aven Interrupter
rows.text: flash, exiles a spell off the stack, and taxes everything they try to cast from exile or graveyards afterwards.

rows.name: Aven Mindcensor
rows.text: flash it onto the fetchland or the tutor.

rows.name: Archivist of Oghma
rows.text: a card and a life every time anybody searches.

rows.name: Swords to Plowshares
rows.text: one mana, exile, unconditional.

rows.name: Generous Gift
rows.text: any permanent, at instant speed.

rows.name: March of Otherworldly Light
rows.text: scalable exile, and the white cards you pitch make it cheap on a locked-out turn.

rows.name: Supreme Verdict
rows.text: uncounterable, and it usually leaves your board — enchantments, artifacts, planeswalkers — untouched.

rows.name: Hullbreaker Horror
rows.text: uncounterable, flash, and every spell you cast afterwards bounces a permanent or an entire spell off the stack. Under a one-spell-per-turn lock this is unbeatable.

rows.name: Approach of the Second Sun
rows.text: the natural finisher for a deck that stops the game. Six mana with Arbiter out, gain seven life, then cast it again seven cards later and win. Note it must be cast FROM YOUR HAND both times.

rows.name: Luminarch Ascension
rows.text: nobody can profitably attack you through Ghostly Prison, so the quest counters accumulate for free. Then it makes a 4/4 flier every turn.

rows.name: Myrel, Shield of Argive
rows.text: her attack trigger doubles your Soldier count every combat. Two attacks after she lands, the board is lethal.

rows.name: Shark Typhoon
rows.text: a flier for every noncreature spell, or cycled at instant speed for an immediate one.

rows.name: Rise and Shine
rows.text: overloaded, every mana rock you control becomes a 4/4. This deck plays a lot of rocks.

rows.name: Cyberdrive Awakener
rows.text: animates every noncreature artifact as a 4/4 AND gives them all flying. Alongside Rise and Shine it is a lethal alpha strike from a board of Signets.

rows.name: Akroma's Will
rows.text: with your commander out, take both halves — the finisher for any of the above.

rows.name: Sakashima of a Thousand Faces
rows.text: copy Grand Arbiter. The legend rule does not apply to your permanents, so you keep both — their spells now cost {2} more and yours {2} less.

rows.name: Spark Double
rows.text: the same trick, and it can copy Jin-Gitaxias or Myrel instead.

rows.name: Multiversal Recruitment
rows.text: a nonlegendary copy of anything you control, twice with flashback.

rows.name: Quantum Misalignment
rows.text: another copy, and rebound makes it two.

rows.name: Rhystic Study
rows.text: in a deck taxing every spell they cast, the extra {1} is rarely available.

rows.name: Mystic Remora
rows.text: the first four turns it is the best card in the deck.

rows.name: Smothering Tithe
rows.text: Treasures that pay for the taxes you have imposed on yourself.

rows.name: Esper Sentinel
rows.text: taxes their first noncreature spell each turn on turn one.

rows.name: Sol Ring
rows.text: the fastest possible start toward a turn-three Arbiter.

rows.name: Lotus Petal
rows.text: fixes and accelerates, and it is free under Sphere of Resistance effects.

rows.name: Mind Stone
rows.text: ramp early, a card later.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep a rock and a tax piece. Sol Ring or a Signet into Thalia, Deafening Silence or Sphere of Resistance on turn two is a far better start than a hand with Approach of the Second Sun in it.

rows.name: Grand Arbiter Augustin IV
rows.text: he is the discount, so land him before you commit to a hand of expensive prison pieces. Four mana on turn three or four, then two pieces a turn afterwards.

Deploy taxes before locks. Sphere of Resistance and Thalia hurt everyone a little; Rule of Law and Sanctum Prelate hurt them a lot — and if you drop the hard lock first, they untap and remove it with the mana the taxes would have eaten.

rows.name: Approach of the Second Sun
rows.text: only start it when the board is actually locked. Seven cards is several turns, and casting the first copy into an open table just tells them what you are doing.
